card_answer: 13 faces have no producer among their visible composers. No harness leaves its bytes behind: 27 of 27 composer sites write the name twice so the original goes back (25 of those inside a finally). Counting only sources other than the harness, 2 faces are written through a helper that receives the composed path, 5 are named by a module constant that reaches a write while the directory half of its composition cannot be resolved, 4 carry the name through local names into a write, 1 are opened for write directly, 0 are passed to a function this scan cannot see and 1 are named by nothing. On the consumer side, 5 faces have a reader that is not the harness (8 states no reader at all) and 1 of those readers assert a field. Retirable under the narrowest rule (no writer, no reader, no name constant): 0 faces / 0 bytes; written by a producer yet read by no consumer: 8 faces / 2781043 bytes. The helper-parameter class: droppedpath_latest.json, producerspill_latest.json
method_limits: author attribution follows direct call sites and one local helper hop; a path composed inside a helper from a module constant and never passed in is still invisible, so B_NONE means 'no source names it', not 'no source writes it'
a reader that goes through a helper is counted as a reader but its block is not priced (e499.price_site needs an opener on the line)
role grading reuses E492's basename regexes; a harness named outside that vocabulary would be graded as a producer
the population is E492's published row set, not a fresh composer scan, so a source added after E492 does not enter this population

sources.note: a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped before parsing; without that, e429_two_hop_writer.py reads as a source that names nothing because ast.parse refuses U+FEFF

title: for every face whose only visible composer is a leg runner: what the harness does with the name, who else writes it, and who reads it
